name: Gotu kola (Centella asiatica)
short: Acute liver failure and death: high rate in a review of 23 herbal liver-injury cases naming gotu kola a top culprit (no gotu kola-only figure). Case reports: hepatitis by mouth, recurring on re-use.
text: Case reports describe three women (aged 49 to 61) who developed jaundice and hepatitis after taking Centella asiatica for 20 to 60 days, with ALT up to 1694 U/L; biopsy showed granulomatous hepatitis in two and chronic hepatitis with cirrhotic transformation in one; all improved after stopping it and receiving ursodeoxycholic acid, and the damage recurred in one woman who took it again. A systematic review of published herb and supplement liver injury reports from Latin America (23 cases) found Centella asiatica among the most reported culprit products, and the series as a whole showed a high rate of acute liver failure and death; the abstract does not give figures for Centella cases separately and notes the difficulty of assessing causality with multi-ingredient products. In contrast, a meta-analysis of randomised trials on cognition and mood (five of Centella asiatica alone and six of products containing it) found that none of the studies reported adverse effects of Centella asiatica, and a 2020 Cochrane review of oral phlebotonics for chronic venous insufficiency (rutosides, hidrosmine and diosmine, calcium dobesilate, Centella asiatica, aminaftone, French maritime pine bark extract and grape seed extract; two of the 56 trials with usable efficacy data were on Centella asiatica) found that phlebotonics as a group probably increase adverse events slightly compared with placebo (risk ratio 1.14, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.27; 37 studies; 5789 participants), most often gastrointestinal, with no separate figures for Centella asiatica. A laboratory study of one water extract in human liver cells and microsomes found no or only weak effects on drug-metabolising P450 enzymes and suggested a low potential for drug interactions; no clinical interaction data were found in the cited sources.
